reason: The E2E sweep treated every explicit profile as a disposable clone and removed PGlite lock/postmaster.pid files before launching. An operator accidentally selecting an active/user profile could remove another runtime's exclusion evidence and increase database corruption/concurrent-open risk; no clone or inactivity proof dominated deletion. The destructive sanitizer is removed. Explicit profiles now fail if either lock entry exists, including dangling links; lock-free dedicated profiles and default scrubbed mkdtemp profiles remain usable. Compatibility: prepare a verified inactive clone or use default scrubbed profile, never delete active-profile locks to satisfy the guard.

evidence.detail: Read-only validation detects both lock entries and refuses to remove them.
Explicit-profile branch runs read-only validator before Electron launch.
Both lock files retain exact bytes on failure; only owned fixture cleanup permits recovery.

reason: Screenshot cleanup previously recursively deleted desktop/narrow children of an unrestricted environment-selected root. A root/home/repository typo or linked output could destroy unrelated local data. It now requires a dedicated bounded non-linked evidence root, rejects linked children and traversal-shaped route IDs, and removes only fixed generated route PNGs plus the fixed manifest, preserving unknown files and nested directories. It is a preventive operator-safety improvement; parent directories must remain operator-owned and not concurrently writable by an adversary.
